beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps a dense carrier while a compact DQ-CTM thought process updates it through shared recurrent ticks.
beats.claim: ThinkSR end to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder.
beats.narration: The method separates dense image structure from the compact thought process that operates on it. The encoder turns the low-resolution image into features. The window step partitions those features for local processing. The DQ-CTM thought process runs recurrent ticks with shared parameters. The decoder turns the updated dense field back into the super-resolved image. The loop returns to the thought stage itself, because the recurrence is within the DQ-CTM ticks.

params.headline: ThinkSR updates a dense carrier with shared recurrent thought ticks
params.note: The recurrence belongs to the thought stage, not the whole flow.

beats.intent: The carrier equation first builds a dense feature field from the low-resolution image, then partitions that field without dropping tokens.
beats.narration: The carrier is the dense object that persists while the thought process reads and updates it. The encoder is the mapping that creates the feature field. The low-resolution image is the input to that mapping. The feature field is the dense spatial carrier. The window partition groups the field while keeping every token.

params.headline: The equation preserves density before thought begins

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model; at 1.129 million parameters it is second largest among the five compared methods.
beats.claim: ×4 lightweight super-resolution, average over five benchmarks.
beats.narration: The parameter comparison should be read as a cost, not as a claim of being cheap. CATANet is the smallest model in this group. RFDN is only slightly larger. IMDN remains under one million parameters. DQ-CTM-SR reaches 1.129 million parameters, making it the second largest of the five. CARN is the largest model in the table.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR is second largest among the five models
